design:
HOST DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-22: the host stood up this session IS the
interop-day host. No fresh EC2 instance.

Caddy-plus-Tailscale is a NORMAL, SUPPORTED way to run mimid, not a
compromise. An earlier version of this note framed it as a problem and
as "foreclosing" an option; Mark pushed back and he was right. The
decision of epic mimid-75nk is "support both", and the reverse-proxy
path is co-equal with mimid terminating TLS itself, not a fallback:

- mimid-server/src/tls.rs implements [trusted_proxy] and documents the
  exact Caddy directive for it;
- mimid-75nk.5 (PKIX mutual TLS) is CLOSED;
- mimid-server/tests/mtls_binaries.rs:1145 is
  pkix_through_a_trusted_proxy(), an end-to-end test of this shape.

Nothing is broken and nothing needs re-architecting.

What the host change actually means:

- NAME: mimi.reviewcommit.com, not mimid.reviewcommit.com. This one is
  permanent: protocol-07 §5.6 puts the hub's identity in the roomId, so
  rooms made here carry this name and cannot be re-homed. Haven must be
  given this name, and the provider key's TXT record published under it.
- PLACE: dokr (10.69.44.52, tailnet 100.87.123.117), not EC2. No new
  security group to build and no world-open SSH to avoid. SSH is
  jrluser@10.69.44.52 on the LAN.
- SHAPE: Caddy on joumon terminates TLS and reverse proxies to
  http://100.87.123.117:8084 (joumon /etc/caddy/Caddyfile:185). So mTLS
  uses the [trusted_proxy] path, which is the point of that feature.

AUDITED ON THE LIVE HOST, 2026-11-22:

Done.
- mimid and mimid-agent both active, binaries built 2026-11-22 16:00,
  after main 677d0d06 (14:29). The code requirements in the description
  are therefore met by the deployed build: mls-extensions-11, the role-1
  list rule (1aa8400), nonces (6dbe357), Room/create roomId.
- TLS and a valid public certificate; /.well-known/jmap answers 401.
- domain, base_url, listen, local_listen, database; [provider_auth]
  dns_servers = 9.9.9.9, 1.1.1.1.
- IRC front end live on the tailnet (100.87.123.117:6667), agent on
  127.0.0.1:8486. One account, mimi://mimi.reviewcommit.com/u/mark,
  zero rooms.

Remaining work. Ordinary configuration, not redesign.

1. PROVIDER SIGNING KEY, and it gates the rest. [provider_auth] carries
   dns_servers and nothing else: no signing key, and no mimid1._mimi TXT
   record exists (checked mimid1._mimi.mimi.reviewcommit.com,
   _mimi.mimi.reviewcommit.com and mimid1._mimi.reviewcommit.com: all
   empty). Without it mimid cannot sign RFC 9421 requests to Haven and
   Haven cannot verify us. Epik must be reached FROM joumon over IPv4
   (curl -4: the signature is registered to joumon's v4 and it egresses
   v6 by default), key from rbw, v2 additive endpoint only -- never v1
   SetHostRecords, which deletes every record.

2. [trusted_proxy] on mimid. Concrete, verified values:
       [trusted_proxy]
       addresses = ["100.81.151.79"]   # jouman-1's tailnet address
       header = "x-client-cert"        # the default
   100.81.151.79 is joumon on the tailnet, confirmed 2026-11-22 as the
   live source of the established connections to 100.87.123.117:8084.
   Forgery is already handled: forwarded_certificate takes the header
   only from the configured addresses and STRIPS it from every other
   source, so another tailnet node cannot claim a certificate it did not
   present.

3. Caddy, on joumon's mimi.reviewcommit.com block:
       client_auth { mode request }
       header_up X-Client-Cert {http.request.tls.client.certificate_der_base64}
   mode request, not require, so ordinary clients are unaffected.

4. [peer_tls]: roots for Haven's server certificate and, for mimid to
   present its own, [peer_tls.identity].

   NOTE the one real operational difference of the proxy path, from
   tls.rs's Limitations: through a proxy only the LEAF certificate
   arrives. Haven's intermediates, if its chain has any, must be in
   mimid's trust configuration rather than arriving in the handshake.
   Check Haven's chain during interop prep.

5. HAVEN PEERING: no peer configured, so no enforce mode and no DNS
   keys. Haven enforcing needs Mark's OK, per the notes.

6. OPENTELEMETRY: no OTEL settings in the unit.

7. mimid-chat: not installed; only mimid and mimid-agent are. The
   description ties Room/create roomId to a matching mimid-chat.

NO SUB-ISSUES FILED: per AGENTS.md, Mark approves a plan before its
sub-issues exist. Items 1 to 7 are the proposed plan.
notes:
2026-11-22, item 1 progress. CORRECTION to the design field: the host is
NOT missing a signing key. mimid generates one on first start and stores
the seed in its database (main.rs:166, store.provider_signing_seed_or_insert),
so mimi.reviewcommit.com has had one since it came up. [provider_auth]
needs no key field and none exists; selector defaults to "mimid1" and
dns_keys defaults to true, so mimid's own configuration needs NO change
for this mechanism. What is missing is only the DNS publication.

Read off the live host with
  sudo mimid admin /etc/mimid/mimid.toml provider-key
(public material only):

  selector   mimid1
  dnsName    mimid1._mimi.mimi.reviewcommit.com
  dnsTxt     v=MIMI1; k=ed25519; p=f/qTeBULmiyoJjRdNjFnRVUAO2Oal3fYbDk7CAjvlgw=

The TXT record to publish, as Epik needs it relative to the
reviewcommit.com zone:

  host  mimid1._mimi.mimi
  type  TXT
  data  v=MIMI1; k=ed25519; p=f/qTeBULmiyoJjRdNjFnRVUAO2Oal3fYbDk7CAjvlgw=

BLOCKED 2026-11-22: rbw is locked on the dev machine, so the Epik API
key cannot be read. Mark unlocks it, then: read the key from rbw, and
from joumon (root@198.71.58.180, key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_joumon) GET the
zone's records first to confirm the endpoint and see what is there, then
POST the single additive create. curl -4 always: the Epik signature is
registered to joumon's IPv4 and joumon egresses IPv6 by default. NEVER
the v1 SetHostRecords method, which replaces the whole record set and
would delete every other record in the zone.

Nothing was left on joumon from the earlier session, by design, so the
call has to be rebuilt rather than replayed from history.
